Switching from Windows to Mac doesn't actually impose that many software restrictions. The platform can run most major computer applications, and there's a large selection of useful Mac-exclusive apps to choose from.

The biggest exception is gaming. However, the latest tests show that Windows games currently perform better on Mac than ever before, whether through official or unofficial channels...

Apple has its own "Game Porting Toolkit" to help developers evaluate how their Windows games run on Mac, aiming to encourage and facilitate game porting to the Mac platform.

However, as Macworld's Filipe Esposito points out, this toolkit is also used by gamers to unofficially run Windows software on Mac—he is one of them. He noted that the latest test version brought significant performance improvements, citing GTA V as an example.

After testing the fourth beta version of the Game Porting Toolkit for several days on a MacBook Pro equipped with an M4 Pro chip, he found that these performance improvements essentially changed the experience of running demanding Windows games... On the same M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory, using the same in-game settings and benchmarks, the frame rate of GTA V increased from approximately 106 fps in the GPTK 3 era to approximately 176 fps in GPTK 4 beta, an increase of about 66%. The game runs quite smoothly at 2K resolution with medium-to-high graphics settings.

He admits that not every game will see such significant improvements, but he hopes these developments will encourage game developers to see Mac as a viable platform.
